seed_ledger.name: Neo Power Generation Facility
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND. No source says how the Neo plant in Jersey Township, Licking County, gets gas. The Ohio Power Siting Board pre-application letter from May 2026 (case 26-0627-EL-BGN) describes 500 MW of simple-cycle units and a 260 MW battery and does not mention a pipeline. Williams calls Neo its fifth Blackstone-funded power project, 682 MW, due in the second half of 2028. Williams says it builds the plants and the gas infrastructure, and the Aristotle pipeline serves several Ohio power projects, but no source ties Aristotle or the Licking County Pipeline to Neo. Aristotle Central, Aristotle South and Licking County Pipeline are already on the roster, so a tie would become a data center tag lead only. Sources checked: the Power Siting Board docket, Williams press releases, the Williams first quarter 2026 earnings recap, trade press, and local news on the Neo open house. The newest EIA workbook, FERC filings and the Ohio EPA air permit showed nothing for this plant. Searches run: 9.

evidence.note: Williams first quarter 2026 recap. Names Neo, 682 MW, second half of 2028. No pipeline named for Neo.

seed_ledger.name: Oregon Energy Park Power Station
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND. No source says how the Capacity Infrastructure plant in Oregon, Lucas County, would get gas. Local and Toledo news say three clusters of 12 generators, 828 MW, over $1 billion, with site details not set. Coverage says only that pipelines run through northwest Ohio. The city rezoned seven parcels. No supplier, lateral or permit filing was found. The Oregon Clean Energy Center and the Vantage campus are different projects. Sources checked: the Power Siting Board, Ohio EPA, FERC, EIA, Columbia Gas of Ohio, city council records, local news, developer material and trade press. Searches run: 8.

seed_ledger.name: Portsmouth Powered Land Project
seed_ledger.reason: NOT_FOUND. No source says how the SB Energy 9.2 GW plant on the Department of Energy site in Piketon, Pike County, would get gas. WOSU, WYSO and Power Magazine coverage describe the plant, a 10 GW data center and AEP Ohio power lines, but no fuel supply. A separate developer, Portsmouth Gas DevCo, has a Power Siting Board notice for up to 2 GW about 5 miles south of Piketon. It is not tied to this plant. An old federal gas contract for the former enrichment site is also not tied to it. Sources checked: the Power Siting Board, Ohio EPA, FERC, EIA, local and trade news, and operator releases. Searches run: 9.
